blocks.heading: A place for social change
blocks.body: From opening its doors in Whitechapel in 1884 to providing free legal advice, discover the people and ideas that shaped Toynbee Hall.

image.alt: Archive photograph of Toynbee Hall’s ivy-covered Victorian buildings, with tall chimneys and gables, around the courtyard.

blocks.heading: Milestones
blocks.intro: Swipe sideways or select a year to explore.

items.title: Toynbee Hall opens
items.body: Henrietta and Samuel Barnett open a university settlement in Whitechapel, where volunteers live and work alongside local people.

image.alt: Engraving of Toynbee Hall’s gabled Victorian building, with tall chimneys and leaded windows.

items.title: The Travellers’ Club
items.body: Language lessons and lectures prepare club members for overseas trips. For many, it’s their first time abroad.

image.alt: Members of the Toynbee Travellers’ Club, in Victorian hats and long skirts, sitting together on a lawn.

items.title: Free legal advice begins
items.body: The Poor Man’s Lawyer service gives East End residents access to legal help they could otherwise struggle to afford.

image.alt: An adviser at his desk talking with a man seated beside him at Toynbee Hall.

items.title: Whitechapel Gallery opens
items.body: The Barnetts’ local exhibitions grow into a permanent gallery, bringing art to more people in East London.

image.alt: Illustration of the Whitechapel Art Gallery’s arched entrance and twin towers, with a horse and cart in the street outside.

items.title: Advice in wartime
items.body: Toynbee Hall hosts one of the first Citizens Advice Bureaux, where residents and volunteers help people with wartime problems.

image.alt: Warden J. J. Mallon leaning over volunteers as they sort wartime food coupons at long tables in the Lecture Hall.

items.title: The historic halls are restored
items.body: A major restoration renews the Victorian halls and helps make the history of Toynbee Hall available through a digital archive.

image.alt: Ashbee Hall, with a long wooden table on a parquet floor beneath tall leaded windows.

items.title: 140 years in the East End
items.body: Toynbee Hall marks its anniversary with an Open House programme that invites the public inside its Victorian halls.

image.alt: Toynbee Hall’s Victorian red-brick building and courtyard garden in East London.

items.title: Meet the Barnetts
items.description: The couple who founded Toynbee Hall.

image.alt: Portrait photograph of Henrietta Barnett, seated, with Samuel Barnett standing beside her.

image.alt: Toynbee Hall’s ivy-covered old library, with a turret and arched doorways, before it was destroyed in the Blitz.
